narrative.overview:
This is not a page that describes infrastructure work; it is a drawing of it, published the way an engineering office publishes a reference architecture. Deep navy ink sits on cool plotter stock. Navy zone fields own whole regions of the page rather than tinting a card. White service plates stand on those fields with visible extruded edges. Rules are hairlines, and they do the separating work that a card, a tinted band, or a shadow would do elsewhere. Every region that carries drawing rather than prose is annotated in a mono drafting hand, and every quantity is set in tabular figures because drafted figures line up in columns.

The density is high and deliberately unpadded. Cells sit shoulder to shoulder separated by a single hairline, produced by laying a one-pixel gap over a rule-coloured ground rather than by bordering each cell — so the grid reads as one ruled sheet, not as a set of tiles that happen to be adjacent. Headings carry their own weight at the top of each sheet; there is no label, kicker, or eyebrow above any heading anywhere in the build, and production status appears as a field inside an evidence block instead. Dark mode is the same poster plotted on a navy ground: a chosen second printing, not an inverted first.

The restraint is a professional posture, not a default. Colour is scarce enough that one blue reads as "energised / live / measured" on sight; the accent appears on discs, rules, figures, and one primary action, and nowhere else. Corners are square by system: the only curves in the whole build are the callout discs, the status dots, and a 3px nub on one measurement bar.
keyCharacteristics: Navy field regions and cool paper regions alternate as full-bleed grounds; nothing floats between them.
Hairline rules and one-pixel grid gaps instead of cards, tints, or dividers with weight.
Depth is drawn as isometric extrusion, never simulated with a shadow on the page surface.
Two hands: Archivo for everything spoken, Azeret Mono for everything annotated.
Square corners everywhere except discs, dots, and a single measurement nub.
Both themes complete and independently declared; neither is a filter over the other.

rules.name: The Two Signals Rule
rules.body: The accent has two declarations, not one: --signal for signal painted on paper, --signal-field for the same role painted on the navy field. They stay separate declarations even in dark mode, where their values coincide, precisely so that darkening one can never silently drag the other below the contrast floor. Never collapse them into a single token, and never paint --signal on a navy ground.

rules.name: The Field Owns The Region Rule
rules.body: A navy field is a full-bleed region that owns everything inside it and sets .on-field so the focus ring inverts. Navy is never a card, never a badge, never a tint behind a paragraph.

rules.name: The Ghost Is Measured Rule
rules.body: The ghost hatch means "the part of the measured whole that is not being claimed". It is a real repeating-gradient hatch on --ghost, and it appears only where a denominator is stated. Never use it as texture.

rules.name: The Drafting Hand Rule
rules.body: Azeret Mono is annotation only — legends, plane and plate labels, dates, quantities, stack chips, and title-block field labels. Interface chrome (nav links, buttons, CTAs, footer) is Archivo. The role line under the name is mono because it is a title-block discipline field, not chrome. Prose is never mono, and code is never rendered at all.

rules.name: The Five Steps Rule
rules.detail: Below the Title step the ramp has five sizes: 10, 11, 12, 15, 17. A new literal font-size is a design decision, not a nudge - if a thing looks wrong at 15px the answer is weight, colour, or spacing, not 14px.

rules.name: The Tabular Figure Rule
rules.body: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums is set on the body, globally and permanently. Drafted figures line up in columns; proportional numerals are the tell that nobody set them.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: Nothing sits above a heading. No eyebrow, no kicker, no label line. Status that would have been an eyebrow ("Running in production") is demoted into an evidence block where it is a stated field rather than a decoration.

rules.name: The Drawn Depth Rule
rules.body: If a surface is part of the sheet, its depth is drawn — extrusion, hairline, or hatch. A shadow on an in-page surface is a bug.

rules.name: The Detached Layer Exception
rules.body: A shadow is permitted only on a node portalled out of flow, only as a soft straight-down diffusion in navy, and only from the two recorded values. A new shadow value is a new layer type; there are two, and there should not be a third.

rules.name: The Leader Hangs Down-Left Rule
rules.body: Diagram annotation hangs down and to the LEFT off a shouldered leader — an isometric run that flattens to a horizontal shoulder before meeting the text, which is how a drafted leader meets its note. The quantity rides inline on the label's own line, in On-Field Signal at weight 600. Never centre a label under a plate; never break the quantity onto a detached second line. Labels carry a knocked-out navy halo (3.5 stroke, paint-order stroke) so the word never fights an edge beneath it.

rules.name: The Removed Share Rule
rules.body: A proportion bar draws the whole measured field. The removed share is the solid Signal span so it matches the headline figure beside it; the remainder is the ghost hatch. The denominator is always stated inline, and all three legend cells — removed, still costs, measured against — must name the same category of quantity. The bar itself is aria-hidden because every value it encodes is written out in the list beside it.

rules.name: The Evidence Marker Rule
rules.body: A filled marker means "appears in the work documented on this page" — never a self-assessed proficiency rating, never a skill bar, never a star. Shipped items sort above unshipped within their group with original order preserved inside each half, the group header carries a plain n of m shipped tally, and both marker states are named in a key. A marker state that isn't keyed is a state the reader has to guess.

rules.name: The Resting State Is Default Rule
rules.body: Every animated element's resting state IS its default style; animations run backwards from a from keyframe. Content is fully present with JavaScript off, with motion reduced, and before any animation runs. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce every keyframe animation is cancelled outright, not shortened.

dos: Do separate surfaces with a hairline rule or a 1px gap over a rule-coloured ground. That is the system's only divider.
Do keep --signal and --signal-field as two separate declarations, and paint each only on its own ground.
Do set annotation, legends, dates, quantities, and title-block field labels in Azeret Mono, and everything spoken — prose and interface chrome — in Archivo.
Do draw depth as isometric extrusion, real gradients, and real hatches.
Do state the denominator whenever a proportion is drawn, and keep all three legend cells naming the same category of quantity.
Do hang diagram annotation down-left off a shouldered leader with the quantity inline on the label's line.
Do keep the lineweight hierarchy: objects heavy (1.9 / 1.4), measurements light (0.75 / 0.6).
Do sort shipped items above unshipped and key both marker states.
Do make every animated element's resting state its default, and cancel animation entirely under reduced motion.
Do replace the isometric drawing with the ruled zone stack below md rather than scaling it down.
donts: Don't put a shadow on any in-page surface. Shadows are permitted only on portalled layers, only from the two recorded values.
Don't use a hard offset shadow, a gradient fill on text, or any simulated physicality anywhere.
Don't put a kicker, eyebrow, or label line above a heading. If the status matters, make it a field in an evidence block.
Don't round a corner. The only curves are callout discs, 6px status dots, and the 3px measurement nub.
Don't draw the remaining share as the solid span — it inverts the claim the headline makes.
Don't treat the evidence marker as a proficiency rating, and never ship a skill bar, percentage, or star scale.
Don't use Azeret Mono for prose, buttons, nav, or the footer, and don't render code or terminal motifs at all.
Don't add a glyph-font icon or a borrowed icon set; the 24x24 / 1.75-stroke family is the only hand.
Don't lay the capability key out in two columns — the ruled ground shows through as an empty half-cell.
Don't set scrollbar-gutter: stable; Radix's scroll lock already pads the body and the two together shift centred content ~7px.
